{{short description|On strongly convergent combinations of a weakly convergent sequence in a Banach space}}
{{no footnotes|date=October 2025}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Mazur's lemma''' is a result in the theory of normed vector spaces introduced by Polish mathematician [[Stanisław Mazur]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bohrium.com/en/sciencepedia/feynman/keyword/mazur_s_lemma |title=Mazur's Lemma |work=bohrium.com |access-date=5 July 2026}}</ref> It shows that any [[Weak topology|weakly convergent]] sequence in a [[Normed vector space|normed space]] has a sequence of [[convex combination]]s of its members that converges strongly to the same limit. Mazur's lemma is used in the proof of [[Tonelli's theorem (functional analysis)|Tonelli's theorem]].

==Statement of the lemma==

{{Math theorem
| name = Mazur's theorem
| math_statement = Let <math>(X, \lVert\cdot\rVert)</math> be a normed vector space and let <math>\left\{x_j\right\}_{j \in \N}\subset X</math> be a sequence which [[weak topology|converges weakly]] to some <math>x\in X</math>.

Then there exists a sequence <math>\left\{y_k\right\}_{k \in \N}\subset X</math> made up of finite convex combination of the <math>x_j</math>'s of the form
<math display="block">y_k=\sum_{j\ge k}\lambda_j^{(k)}x_j</math>
such that <math>y_k\to x</math> strongly that is <math>\lVert y_k-x\rVert\to 0</math>.
}}

For a proof see Ekeland & Temam (1974), p. 6.
